newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Police may take on Australia senator investigation.
newsitem.headline: Police may take on Australia senator investigation.

text.p: Australian Senate President Margaret Reid, examining fraud allegations against key independent senator Mal Colston, told the upper house on Wednesday she may call in the police.

She had now asked for official legal advice on whether she should ask the police to look at the wrongful expense claims of Colston, which Senate officers discovered in an investigation reported on Monday.
"In the light of matters referred to in the reports I must now consider whether those matters should be referred to the Australian Federal Police for further investigation," she said.
Colston, a Labor defector on whom the government must rely for controversial legislation, conceded on Monday he had wrongly claimed travel allowance in recent years, but only by mistake.
The Labor party says his excuse of poor bookkeeping is implausible and has called for further examination of his claims.
Colston's survival is crucial for the Liberal-National government's economic reform programme, because almost all other parties in the upper house are left-leaning.
The government is two votes short of a majority in the Senate and those two votes are often available only from Colston and the other independent.
Colston could not sit in parliament if convicted of fraud.
Since he was originally elected as a Labor candidate, he would be replaced by a Labor member, critically changing the balance of power in the Senate.
Reid published advice from the chief executive of her department, Clerk of the Senate Harry Evans, who said that his staff should not conduct any further investigation.
Guidelines directed her to seek the advice of the Attorney-General's Department on what to do, he said.
